result.summary: Rejects node startup with an initialization error if -port=65535 and the onion service bind port must be derived from it. The node now checks that default_bind_port is below UINT16_MAX before computing the default onion port, while continuing to allow -port=65535 when an explicit onion port is specified or when listening is disabled.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core derives the default Tor onion service bind port by adding 1 to -port. When -port is set to 65535, the uint16_t addition wraps to 0, causing the node to bind 127.0.0.1 on an arbitrary OS-assigned ephemeral port and point the automatic Tor onion service there.
evidence: Commit message and description explain the integer overflow: 'The default onion bind uses -port + 1. With -port=65535 this wraps to 0, so the node binds 127.0.0.1 to a random port and the automatic onion service points there.'
result.changed_since_previous: Diff is now available; the implementation and functional test coverage match the earlier description.
result.card: Bitcoin Core calculates the default Tor onion service bind port as -port + 1. When -port is set to 65535, the uint16_t addition wraps to 0, causing the node to bind 127.0.0.1 to an arbitrary OS-assigned ephemeral port for its automatic onion service. This change fails initialization with a descriptive error when -port=65535 and an onion port needs to be derived. Explicit onion bind configurations (-bind=<addr>:<port>=onion) and disabled listening (-listen=0) continue to work.

risk.why: A flaw would cause node initialization to fail incorrectly on valid port configuration arguments.
